expectations: Both DEBT markers (queue.js and lookup.py) are found and reported, each with its what/ceiling/upgrade fields intact

The queue.js entry is identified as due/fired: deploy.config.json's workerProcesses: 2 satisfies its stated upgrade trigger of running behind a second worker process, and the response calls this out distinctly from ordinary debt

No unmarked code in the fixture (e.g. drain() in queue.js or the module exports) is reported as a debt entry — only actual DEBT: markers are harvested
